Definition: from G1223 and G1841; an outlet through, i.e. probably an open square (from which roads diverge):--highway.
BiblicalUsage: The highways are the streets and the crossroads, the places where the crowds pass, and the word stands once, in the parable of the wedding feast. The servants are sent into the highways to gather all they find, both bad and good, and the wedding is furnished with guests.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the highways are where the gospel goes; the invited guests refused, so the servants went to the crossroads, and the feast was filled with people no one expected to see there.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
